# Requirement Traceability Matrix (RTM) — {PROJECT_NAME}

**Version:** 1.0.0
**Last Updated:** {YYYY-MM-DD}
**Purpose:** Trace every requirement from its source, through classification and priority, to the
user story that implements it and the test case that verifies it — so any requirement's status
can be answered in one lookup instead of a search through chat history.

> Update this file whenever a requirement is added, changed, or a linked user story/test case is
> created. A stale RTM is worse than none — it gives false confidence that coverage is tracked.

---

## How to use this matrix

- **ID** — matches the ID used in `docs/planning/FSD.md` (BR-, SR-, FR-, NFR-, TR- prefixes)
- **Priority** — MoSCoW: Must / Should / Could / Won't (this release)
- **Status** — Draft / Verified / Signed-off / In Development / Testing / Done / Deferred
- Leave a cell as `—` rather than deleting the column if not yet applicable — an empty cell is a
  visible gap; a missing column hides it

## Coverage Summary

*(Regenerate this section whenever the matrix is updated — it's the fastest way to spot a gap)*

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| Total requirements | {N} |
| Must-have requirements | {N} |
| Must-have requirements with a linked user story | {N} / {N} |
| Must-have requirements with a linked test case | {N} / {N} |
| Requirements still in Draft status | {N} |
| Requirements with unresolved dependencies | {N} |

**Rule of thumb:** Before development starts on a module, every Must-have requirement in that
module should have a Related User Story. Before that module is marked Ready to Deliver, every
Must-have requirement in it should have a Test Case ID and a Status of at least Testing.
